reels.caption: There are a lot of bars in London that claim to be hidden, but this one is a true hidden bar! 👀 📍 @221b  #foodanddrink

LONDON’S FIRST HUGE SANDO (JAPNAESE SANDWICH) HIDDEN GEM 😍🥵!!

So, we finally found an amazing Sando spot. This place is a serous hidden gem that more people need to talk about. They’re doing something special with classics, and honestly, it’s a breath of fresh air. It’s not just about the eats; it’s an experience, and a darn good one.

Sandos (Japanese Style Sandwiches):
The bread’s thick, like really thick, and the fillings, especially the (super juicy) pulled beef and my go-to, the breakfast burger, are something else. The bacon and egg combo is just magical, and their halal bacon – hands down, the best texture and taste.

Smashburgers:
Let’s talk smash burgers. The meat’s got the most spot on fat ratio. You gotta try it to understand.

Triple Fried Chips:
And the triple-fried chips – man, they’re a game-changer. Crunchy on the outside, soft inside, and they’re some of the best fat chips you’ll find in the UK. Solid 10/10 – they won me over.

Loaded Triple Fried Fries:
- Butter chicken loaded fries – never expected to see this on a menu. Taking an authentic comfort dish and turning it into loaded fries was a stroke of brilliance. Damn good!

- Poutine is rare in the UK, but they nailed it. Real cheese curds, gravy that’s seasoned to perfection – I finally found poutine that hits the spot!

Slow Roasted Lamb Neck:
Now, the slow-roasted lamb neck – it’s not your usual find on menus, but wow, was it soft. Fell off the bone soft. Honestly, didn’t see that coming.

✅ Overall rating: 9.5/10
✅ Fully halal (no alcohol on site)

I don’t hand out 9.5/10’s lightly, but @chipsy_uk have earned it.

It’s not just about the food; it’s about the passion and creativity. From the sandwiches to the fries and the unexpected lamb neck. If you’re looking for somewhere that nails every dish, this is it.

A slightly sweet brioche bun, filled with freshly whipped chantilly cream & traditionally dusted with icing sugar, here you have the option to dip it in pistachio or chocolate too😫😍

These were heavenly!! The brioche bun was soft, slightly sweet & the cream was light, so smooth & also just the right amount of sweet. My favourite flavour was the chocolate. It just added a little something different, especially with the crushed chips on top😍

But these were the 4 that spoke to me the most and are now on my shortlist

Hersh Al Asof from Al Ezz Oud – Pure luxury, a citrus open, creamy middle and a smoky, woody earthy dry down

Black Forest from Al Ambra – A very clean woody citrus and for me personally I preferred this to Dubai Musk

Frankel Silver from Assaf– One of the nicest takes on Virgin Island water I have tried

The 4th was another Assaf, Swimming in Summer and a full review to follow on that as I purchased it!

20 Minutes from the centre of London it really isn’t that far to travel, I mean even @fbfragrances has popped in and signed a bottle of @_rasasiofficial Hawa Sapphire, and he lives in Australia . SADDLE FROM DUBAI DROPPED IN LONDON AND I AM SO EXCITED 😍!!

If you haven’t heard of Saddle from the UAE, they recently opened in London, right near Harrods and went viral as the Ruler of Dubai, Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, was spotted there 🇦🇪!

While their other locations have a large menu, the London spot is more of a cosy café with a more focused all-day breakfast menu.

Everything is fully halal ✅

Starting with the drinks, the specialty coffee here is lovely. The latte was just right—not too heavy or light, making it a perfect pick-me-up.

The pistachio milkshake was a surprise—rich, creamy, yet not overly heavy - 8.9/10.

Onto the food.

Breakfast Brioche Sandwiches; the highlight. They all come with a scrambled eggs base. I must say, the eggs were cooked beautifully—silky, creamy, and not dry at all.

My top picks are the “Saddle La Brioche” and the Bacon & Cheese, which uses veal bacon. I much prefer it to turkey bacon. Overall, I’d rate the brioche sandwiches an 8.5/10.

Grilled cheese sandwich had Turkish cheese in it. I’m not usually a fan, but this was good—cheesy and well-balanced, 7.9/10.

Creamy truffle mushroom toast was a real winner. The mushroom flavour was strong and paired perfectly with the truffle, 8.5/10.

Zaatar Labneh AvoToast was unique and something you don’t often find. It was decent, but I’d rate it a 7.5/10 as it lacked that ‘wow’.

Crepes— had a good variety with an Omani-inspired chips and cheese option. They were all quite tasty. The pistachio crepe was my favourite, with the lemon and sugar version coming in close second with its refreshing zest, 8/10.

My top recommendations are the “Saddle La Brioche” and Bacon & Cheese brioche, Mushroom Toast, the pistachio milkshake & pistachio crepe.

Given its convenient location and reasonable prices, overall 8/10. 

📍 7 Montpelier St, London, SW7 1EX

Forever one of my favourite brunch spots and London food spots overall. It’s one of those places where substance and style are equally yoked. Reconfirmed my love for Milk Cafe after a long-overdue visit, where I got to try their banana bread for the first time. It was nothing short of legendary. 

4) @gunpowder_london - Soho, Spitalfields, Tower Bridge

A restaurant I’ve wanted to try for yeeeeeears and 2023 was the year I popped my Gunpowder cherry. From the cocktails to the food, everything was genuinely really good - but that bread and butter pudding? One of the best desserts I’ve had in London. If a warm hug had a taste, it would be that pudding. 

3) Reindeer Cafe @wingyipstore - Cricklewood

One of my favourite hidden gems in London. I’ve been shopping at Wing Yip for years so I always knew about their restaurants but never had an opportunity to try it. Reindeer Cafe is always busy and for good reason. Delicious Cantonese food at decent prices, making it an elite post-grocery munch spot.

2) @sonora.ldn - Stoke Newington

My favourite new restaurant opening in 2023. Been a big fan of Sonora Taqueria ever since I tried their tacos in 2022 when they were still based in @netilmarket. Now they’re slinging authentic Sonoran tacos down in Stoke Newington and suddenly, moving to Stoke Newington has never been so appealing to me. 

1) @fallowrestaurant - St James’s (AD PR)

Fallow is that girl. Super hyped on socials, but it deserves the hype. I loved their attention to detail (still obsessed with the plating of their cabbage) and that each dish was as flavoursome as the last. I’ve eaten really well this year, but my meal at Fallow definitely stood out the most for me.

I had a jug of their rum punch and was already feeling a bit tipsy before the food arrived 😅. My friend had their Lychee Rose Martini which was nice too 😋. I love that their Sunshine Rum Punch, Guinness Punch & Peanut Punch are all vegan 🌱

We did have a little bit of food left at the end but was told it was £10 to take food away so we ended up leaving it 🥲

All of the food came out piping hot each time and I would say the wait times were similar to à la carte dining restaurants. I loved the range of food options and that you can order as many plates as you want at a time 🙌🏽

Octaves Kitchen played Reggae while we were there and it was just the perfect atmosphere. I will 10000% be going back again; it’s such great value for money 🤩

Right off the bat, their unit in the shopping centre is massive, with ample seating, including cute booths at one end of their restaurant. Service, atmosphere and cleanliness were top notch🙌🏻

For the £19 Iftar set menu, you get a main (choose between burgers, chicken tenders or sandwiches), fries (regular or peri peri), juice and a petite dessert 🍮 

From the mains we tried the cheese-licious cheese burger, which was our favourite. It actually reminded me of Salt in DXB (controversial I know 😂) - it was really tasty 🍔 we also tried the classy chick fried chicken burger, which was also delicious 🍗 finally we tried the ultimate club sandwich- the filling was good but the actual bread was a bit basic (just normal white toast) 🥪 so I would stick to the burgers!

Onto the star of the show- the petit desserts. You can choose from a french toast, croffle or a waffle, with 4 flavours to choose from each one 🤤 for the french toast we had the lotus one, which was absolutely amazing- I thought I was sick of lotus but this re-kindled my love 🍞 the croffle was my personal favourite (it’s a croissant waffle) which we got in caramel flavour- it has a unique taste to it and a crunch 🥐 the waffle was also so good, it was made fresh and wasnt chewy at all like i’ve had from other places 🧇 

I think for £19 this was an amazing offer, and you can even have it for a post-taraweeh meal too 🙏🏼

TRYING NORTH LONDON’S FAMOUS DESI PUB 🇮🇳 🍛 

Tamil Prince have established a reputation of class and it’s only been open for a couple of years. A former old pub has been refurbished to serve cracking Indian small plates and amazing roti’s. I wouldn’t say this comes across as a ‘boozer’, where you’ll go and stand onsite with a bees hive of people. It’s more of a restaurant and I imagine in the summer people will congregate around the seating outside. 

Love how you can see into the kitchen to see the chefs are work. The wood was all very good. The onion baji’s, the dosa, the ocra fries, lamb chops and the paneer butter masala were my favs but everything had a lovely level of space was cooked perfectly. 

They have just opened a second spot too @the_tamil_crown which isn’t far away and they serve up an Indian inspired roast every Sunday which looks class.

I remember going to @the_tamil_prince with a lot of speculation, however, being absolutely blown away by everything 🤤 Ad

Former Roti King chef Prince Durairaj alongside ex-JKS GM Glen Leeson have launched this pub together with a South Indian focused menu but with a classic British pub vibe. The elegancy with which they have combined the two elements together is just exceptional 👏🏽 

✨ WHAT WE HAD ✨

👉🏾 Chicken lollipop with sweet chilli chutney - £10.50
👉🏾 Prince’s special masala - £7.50
👉🏾 Channa bhatura with raita - £10.50
👉🏾 Robata lamb chops - £33.00
👉🏾 Thanjuvar chicken curry - £13.00

I am used to visiting local family run South Indian restaurants almost once a week (I don’t joke when I say it’s my favourite food) so I was trying to hold Tamil Prince in the same comparison. For me, the flavours were outstanding of each and every thing!

I haven’t seen lamb chops feature much in South Indian cuisine (correct me if I’m wrong) but the ones we tried here were SOOOO good 🤌🏾🤤 The chicken curry was BANG on and the pairing of that flaky roti with it made it taste so much better.

This place is on the pricier side which was the only negative factor for me because I am used to paying £5 for mains at my local South Indian restaurants meanwhile the prices for mains went up to £33 here. Would I still recommend you to visit here? Absolutely! Give it a try - the money is definitely worth spending! 

✨ Halal (although alcohol is served on site)

A drink and a dessert in one? Perfect for the warmer weather! 

1:📍Xing Fu Tang - Frith Street, Chinatown

📝my order: 
🧋 brown sugar boba milk with dalgona coffee [£4.75]🧋 brown sugar boba milk tea [£4.95]

There is always a long queue, but service is really speedy. Be aware that the classic brown sugar boba milk is exactly that - literally flavoured milk (and WAY too sweet). But the tea and coffee versions? Beautiful🤩

The sugary tapioca is chewy and fresh - you can tell by how warm it feels at the bottom of your cup. It complements the bitterness of the dalgona and tea so well. 

✅rating: 9/10! I’d love if we could customise the sugar levels in the drinks a bit more. 
{#gifted}

2:📍Knoops - Leicester Square 

📝my order: 
🥤54% iced chocolate with sea salt [£4.95]

This is such a cute café in the heart of Leicester Square! The 21 drink options are for the hot chocolates which I will absolutely come back to try. For iced drinks, you choose from about 6 options, but the workers are so nice and let you try the chocolate (blended or just straight-up) before you make your decision. 

The drink was creamy and delicious. And all their toppings are made fresh in-house, too! 

I’ve heard their hot chocolates are even better, so I’ll definitely be back👀

✅rating: 10/10!

reels.caption:
Save these 7 unforgettable experiences for your London trip.

1. @zip_world_london 
The longest and tallest tunnel slide in the world is at @zip_world_london and it’s epic! Minimum height is 1.3 metres. Take the tube to Stratford. It’s near Westfield shopping centre. Book via link in bio on @zip_world_london 

2. @ifly_london 
This is soooo much fun. The video is of the instructor - I wish I looked that good when I tried it. Minimum age is 3. It’s at the @theo2london book via @ifly_london 

3. @hangloose_bluewater 
I know this isn’t London but it’s just a short trip and so worth the journey! Try Europe’s largest swing. It’s unforgettable! It’s at Bluewater in Kent. Minimum age is 8 but there’s also a minimum weight requirement of 35kg. Book via @hangloose_bluewater 

4. @thamesrockets 
This is one of my favourite things to do in London. There’s no age restriction on the ultimate London adventure ticket. It leaves from the London Eye pier on the South Bank. Book via @thamesrockets 

5. Glass floor at @towerbridge is so cool and it’s great for all the family. There are lifts to the top of the bridge if you need them or you can take the stairs. This is one of my favourite things we’ve done in London. All ages welcome. Book via link in bio on @towerbridge 

6. @upattheo2 
I’ve done this in the day time and night time. Try to get a sunset or night climb if you can - it was beautiful with all the lights. Minimum age is 8. Book via @upattheo2 

7. @tottenhamhotspurstadium 
Walk up the Spurs stadium on the Dare Skywalk and then choose to either walk back down or abseil off the top. Minimum  height is 1.2 metres. Minimum age for the abseil is 12.
